clue.text: Doctor welcoming start of lovely old musical

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the doctor word holds the other pieces inside it
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A doctor fond of a charming old stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDIC opens to take in L and O: ME(LO)DIC. 'Musical' looks like a show but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something melodic has a pleasing tune, which is what makes a sound or piece musical.

clue.text: Planners principally mark original papers

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so the opening letter is kept
something original is newly made, so the letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Planners marking up the original documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Mappers draw up charts and layouts, so they plan out territory or routes in diagram form.

clue.text: Immature insect — some particular variety

indicators.note: some means a portion only, so the answer is part of the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A young bug of one specific species.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in particuLAR VAriety.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the grub stage of an insect between hatching and pupation, before adulthood.

clue.text: Black Beauty say, competitor about whom little is known

definitions.note: a definition by example: Black Beauty is a famous fictional black horse
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a horse of black colour, as in Anna Sewell's novel

definitions.text: competitor about whom little is known
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an unfancied contestant of unknown ability

explanation.walkthrough: Black Beauty is the black horse of Anna Sewell's classic children's novel; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a contender whose ability is hidden, and taken literally it describes a black-coated horse.

clue.text: Bashful cat half consumed large rodent

indicators.note: with half eaten away, only half of that word survives

explanation.surface: A shy cat that has eaten half of a big rat.
explanation.walkthrough: PUSS loses its second half to leave PU.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a big South American water rodent, also called nutria, farmed for fur.

clue.text: Manured incorrectly without accessory apparatus

indicators.note: done incorrectly means put together wrongly, so the letters come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Muck spread badly on a field, done without the proper equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: In botany and zoology an unarmed plant or animal lacks thorns, spines or claws, the 'accessory apparatus' of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unarmed means lacking weapons, and in biology lacking spines or claws, the extra defensive equipment some organisms carry.

clue.text: Is endured unhappily, not wanted

indicators.note: things going unhappily are in a bad way, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Something put up with grudgingly because nobody wants it.
explanation.definitionFit: Undesired describes something nobody wishes for, an unwelcome or unrequested thing.

clue.text: Appeal I binned contains self-justification

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within it, so the letters are found inside those words

parts.note: the letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A rejected appeal that still holds an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in appeAL I BInned.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is an excuse, strictly a claim to have been elsewhere, offered to clear oneself of blame.

clue.text: Mother sings softly clasping American cookies

indicators.note: to clasp something is to hold it tight, so the singing word grips the other letter inside

parts.note: to croon is to sing in a soft, low voice
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Mum humming while she holds American biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cookies' is the American word for what Britons call biscuits, which ties in with the American in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroons are small almond-and-egg-white biscuits, cookie being the American word for a biscuit.

clue.text: Speaks with contempt of empty daytime journeys

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of daytime

explanation.surface: Sneering at pointless daytime trips.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule, treating someone with scorn in what one says.

clue.text: Wine and fish journalist described in words

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A food writer describing a meal of wine and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something is to depict it, and portraying can be done verbally as well as in paint.

clue.text: Suffer fashionable dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A trendy pet dog that has to put up with things.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it upon yourself and have to bear it.

clue.text: Revolutionary maths aces embracing electronic financial transactions

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the hidden letters are read backwards
something embracing holds it in its arms, so the answer sits inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Brilliant mathematicians who are pioneers of digital money.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiding in matHS ACEs, read right to left, is E-CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: E-cash is money held and spent digitally, so it covers payments made over electronic networks.

clue.text: Break stride and run for Bond's martini?

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: the two words of fodder joined by 'and'

explanation.surface: A runner breaking stride and dashing off for a James Bond cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: James Bond famously orders his martini 'shaken, not stirred'; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond insists his martini be shaken rather than mixed with a spoon, so the drink must be left unmixed that way.

clue.text: Royals are out of sorts in period of revolution

indicators.note: out of sorts means disordered and unwell, so the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: The royal family is feeling grumpy during a time of political upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests uprising, but it is the Earth's orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar year is the time the Earth takes to complete one orbit around the Sun.

clue.text: Modern but sadly tardy and late

indicators.note: things going sadly have gone wrong, so the letters end up jumbled

parts.note: the two words of fodder joined by 'and'

explanation.surface: Up to date, yet regrettably always running late.
explanation.definitionFit: Latter-day means belonging to recent or present times, a current version of something older.

clue.text: European questions about right royal attendants

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: about means around, so the questions word goes round the other letter

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A European asking pointed questions about some very grand servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right royal' reads as the idiom meaning thorough, but 'right' is R. E then QUERIES around R.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer of the British royal household who personally assists a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Kicks fellow doing menial hotel tasks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: strikes with the foot
second meaning: the old name for a hotel servant who cleaned shoes and carried bags

explanation.surface: A hotel porter lashing out with his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means delivers a blow with the foot; the noun is a traditional British term for a hotel's shoe-cleaning servant.

clue.text: Give detailed analysis of reason car won't go

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a verb phrase standing for the noun as in 'give a breakdown'; the setter treats the answer as the thing given.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means an itemised analysis of figures and also a mechanical failure that stops a vehicle.

clue.text: Dip discovered in combat helmet

indicators.note: something discovered inside is found lying within, so the answer is found inside the words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A dent or hollow found in a soldier's helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in comBAT HElmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip is a quick swim, and to bathe is to go swimming or immerse oneself in water.

clue.text: Of good pedigree and full of life?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of pure breeding, as with livestock
second meaning, playfully: filled with blood, the stuff of life

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second sense: blood is the fluid of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooded animals are of fine breeding, and the word literally suggests having blood, the vital fluid, in the veins.

clue.text: Stripped like a plain salad

definitions.meaning: first meaning: with clothes taken off
second meaning: served without any oil-and-vinegar topping

explanation.surface: Someone naked, as bare as a salad with nothing on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means naked, and also describes salad leaves served with no vinaigrette poured over them.

clue.text: Resentment of last of men becoming trapped ultimately in underground cell

indicators.note: one thing becoming another means it is swapped out, so one letter is exchanged for a different one

parts.note: a dungeon is an underground prison cell

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter of the word before it is taken

explanation.surface: The bitterness of men locked away in a dark cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: In DUNGEON the N changes to D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offended indignation, usually met in the phrase 'in high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Series of six balls in cricket surprisingly worth upset

parts.words: Series of six balls in cricket
parts.note: in cricket a bowler delivers six balls per over

indicators.note: something that happens surprisingly comes out unexpectedly, so the letters emerge in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A cricket over that unexpectedly proves its value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overthrow' is also a cricket term, which strengthens the misleading surface; here it is the verb meaning to topple.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow a government or leader is to topple them, and upset can mean knock over or defeat.

clue.text: Suitable moment, it's said, for plant used for seasoning

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: the right time is a suitable moment

explanation.surface: The right moment to add herbs while cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a low aromatic herb whose leaves are used to flavour food.

clue.text: Swallow's tail, covering birds, flutters

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: Aves is the Latin name for the class of birds

explanation.surface: A swallow's forked tail fluttering over a flock of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the W sits on top of AVES, so it is 'covering' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag waves when it moves to and fro in the breeze, much as something flutters.

clue.text: Requirement we're told, to massage

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: Someone saying they really need a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working dough or muscles by pressing and squeezing them with the hands.

clue.text: Venerator embraces love-poetry muse

indicators.note: a word that embraces something holds it within, so the answer lies inside it

explanation.surface: An admirer hugging the goddess of romantic verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in vENERATOr; a venerator is one who reveres.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one who presides over lyric and amorous poetry.

clue.text: Parent to join with others between beginning and end of day

indicators.note: placed between two things means set inside them, with one on either side
the beginning and end of a word are its first and last letters, so only those two are kept

parts.note: to add is to join something on with others

explanation.surface: A parent spending the whole day with the family.
explanation.walkthrough: ADD sits between D and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy is a familiar, childish word for a father, who is one kind of parent.

clue.text: Popular stringed instrument, item at heart safe from injury

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: the heart of something is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

explanation.surface: A popular string instrument kept safe and undamaged at the centre of a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Inviolate means unharmed, untouched or not violated, so kept free of damage or breach.

clue.text: Chide about Yankee essentially banal sobriety

indicators.note: about means around, so the scolding word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to dress, as in give a dressing-down, is to scold
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: the essence of a word is at its core, so only the central letter is kept

explanation.surface: Scolding an American for being dull and teetotal.
explanation.walkthrough: To dress someone down, or give them a dressing-down, is to tell them off, which is why the word can mean chide.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryness can mean abstaining from alcohol, as in a dry state or dry January, which is sobriety.

clue.text: Outspoken child sad when day is at an end

definitions.text: when day is at an end

indicators.note: outspoken words are uttered out loud, so the next word is taken by how it is heard

explanation.surface: A blunt-talking child gloomy at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is sunset, the evening time at which daylight finishes.
